articles.title: Jim Cramer Calls Out 'Pretty Thick' Negativity on Apple, Palantir and Marvell: 'No Matter What They Say, It Isn't Enough'
articles.summary: View more earnings on AAPL CNBC’s Jim Cramer is not buying Monday’s selloff in Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL), Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ:PLTR) and Marvell...
articles.body:
CNBC's Jim Cramer is not buying Monday's selloff in Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ: PLTR ) and Marvell Technology Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL ) as the tech slump stretches into a new week.

In a post on X, Cramer said that investors are piling "negativity" onto the three tech stocks and that it is "pretty thick."

"No matter what they say, it isn't enough…" he added.

The negativity when it comes to Marvell, Apple, Palantir is pretty thick… No matter what they say, it isn't enough… — Jim Cramer (@jimcramer) November 2, 2026

The negativity when it comes to Marvell, Apple, Palantir is pretty thick… No matter what they say, it isn't enough…

Jim Cramer (@jimcramer) November 2, 2026

Marvell shares fell more than 12% on Monday after it announced an all-stock deal to buy Lumentum Holdings Inc. for $115 billion, and the stock has lost about $70 billion in market value since reports of the deal surfaced on Oct. 28.

Last week's two-day tech rout erased more than $600 billion in market value from Alphabet Inc. and Intel Corp. as investors punished cash-draining spending on artificial intelligence.

AAPL Beats, but Margin Guide Disappoints

Apple reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $114.48 billion, above the $113.39 billion estimate, according to Benzinga Pro data, while earnings per share came in at $2.10 per share, versus $1.98 expected

Apple guided December-quarter gross margin to 45% to 46%, down from 47.9%, which included a 1-point tariff-refund benefit. It said most of the decline is expected to come from higher memory costs.

Futurum Equities' Shay Boloor said the memory chip boom lifting Micron Technology Inc. and SK Hynix Inc. is squeezing Apple, with on-device AI likely to require even more memory per iPhone.

$AAPL said gross margins excluding tariff refunds were "down about 1 point sequentially, primarily driven by higher memory costs" extending a decline to 47% in September. The irony is that DRAM boom benefiting $MU and $SKHY is squeezing Apple just as its push into on-device AI… pic.twitter.com/4DBXNaTT9C — Shay Boloor (@StockSavvyShay) November 2, 2026

$AAPL said gross margins excluding tariff refunds were "down about 1 point sequentially, primarily driven by higher memory costs" extending a decline to 47% in September. The irony is that DRAM boom benefiting $MU and $SKHY is squeezing Apple just as its push into on-device AI… pic.twitter.com/4DBXNaTT9C

Shay Boloor (@StockSavvyShay) November 2, 2026

Palantir beat on both lines in the third quarter, reporting revenue of $2.31 billion against estimates of $2.18 billion and adjusted earnings of 44 cents per share against 41 cents.

The stock closed 3% lower and fell 2.99% in extended trading.

However, investors focused on the company's U.S. commercial bookings, where growth in total contract value slowed to 11% year over year from more than 153% in the previous quarter.

articles.title: US factory orders beat expectations in September amid broad strength
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Nov 3 (Reuters) - New orders for US factory goods increased more than expected in September, boosted by bookings for aircraft and a range of othe...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Nov 3 (Reuters) - New orders for US factory goods increased more than expected in September, boosted by bookings for ‌aircraft and a range of other goods, government data showed ‌on Tuesday.

Factory orders rose 1.8% after an upwardly revised 0.3% gain in August, the ​Commerce Department's Census Bureau said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast orders surging 1.2% after a previously reported 0.1% gain in August.

Orders advanced 7.2% on a year-over-year basis in September.

An artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout and ‌strong consumer spending are ⁠anchoring manufacturing, which accounts for about 9.4% of the economy.

But economists have cautioned that rising interest rates and ⁠declining inflation-adjusted household income would hamper manufacturing activity next year, especially the segments not exposed to the AI spending frenzy.

Though an Institute for Supply ​Management survey ​on Monday showed production at factories ​booming in October, sentiment among ‌manufacturers continued to deteriorate, with pricing volatility, longer lead times, tariffs and the US-Israeli war with Iran cited as major drags.

Factory orders in September were driven by 28.3% jump in bookings for the volatile civilian aircraft and parts component. Orders for motor vehicle bodies, parts ‌and trailers edged up 0.1%. Machinery orders ​soared 1.5%. Orders for computers and electronic ​products rose 0.8%, and ​vaulted 14.9% year over year.

Orders for electrical equipment, appliances ‌and components fell 0.3%. The Census ​Bureau also reported ​that orders for non-defense capital goods excluding aircraft, which are seen as a measure of business spending plans on equipment, increased ​0.6% in September ‌instead of 0.5% as reported last month.

Shipments of these so-called ​core capital goods shot up 1.2% as initially estimated.

(Reporting by ​Lucia Mutikani; Editing by Andrea Ricci)

articles.title: What a Democratic sweep could mean for stocks — and why history says not much
articles.summary: Every midterm outcome under a Republican president has left the S&P 500 about 15% higher a year later.
articles.body:
Polls and prediction markets have spent weeks pointing to a Democratic sweep. History says the outcome has shaped stocks for about three months, then barely at all.

That may surprise anyone bracing for a long night of maps and swing counties. Polymarket gave Democrats a 76% chance of winning both the House and the Senate as of Tuesday morning, with a Democratic House and a Republican Senate a distant second at 19%.

The House looks like the surer bet. The Senate is where the drama is. Republicans hold it 53-47, Democrats need a net gain of four seats, and polling models and prediction markets differ more on that chamber . Some races may not be called Tuesday night.

Since 1946, midterms under a Republican president have ended three of the four ways Congress can go. A year later, the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) was up an average of 15% to 16% after each one, according to Yahoo Finance calculations from the Election Day close. Over the long run, Wall Street's verdict has been bipartisan.

The short run is a different story. After the seven midterms that left Democrats running Congress, stocks rose an average of 11% over the next three months and were higher every time. After the lone Republican hold, in 2002, stocks fell 8% as the US moved toward war with Iraq. By the end of each president's term, all three outcomes were up on average.

None of this carries much statistical muscle. A Democratic sweep has happened seven times under a Republican president, a Democratic House with a Republican Senate twice, and a Republican hold once. A Republican House with a Democratic Senate has never happened.

Even the sweep record needs a footnote. In five of those seven years, Democrats already ran Congress. Only twice did a Republican president lose both chambers, as Democrats are trying to make happen this year — in 1954 under Dwight Eisenhower and in 2006 under George W. Bush. Stocks rose about 33% and 7% over the following year.

And the ride can get bumpy. The last time President Trump lost the House, in 2018, the S&P 500 sank nearly 15% by Christmas Eve as the Federal Reserve raised rates and trade tensions with China escalated. Then it bounced, finishing about 12% higher a year after the midterm election. The 2006 sweep by Democrats ran into the financial crisis, leaving stocks down about 38% by the time Bush left office in 2009.

Blue, red or divided, the S&P 500 was higher a year after all 20 midterms since 1946, measured from Election Day, with an average gain of about 14%. The closest call was 1946 itself, a gain of just 0.1%. The streak lines up with the strongest stretch of the presidential cycle , which runs from late in a midterm year into the next.

articles.title: BMW issues second profit warning in a year
articles.summary: Premium German carmaker BMW issued its second profit warning for the financial year on Tuesday, citing costs related to job cuts as well as a production ramp...
articles.body:
Premium German carmaker BMW issued its second profit warning for the financial year on Tuesday, citing costs related to job cuts as well as a production ramp-up.

The core profit margin at the cars business was now seen at between minus 0.5 percent to plus 0.5 percent in 2026, BMW said, meaning it could make an operating loss in its key activity.

That compares to a core profit margin of between one and three percent which the Munich-based manufacturer expected back in June, itself a cut on expectations at the start of the year.

Like its peers, BMW has struggled with cutthroat competition and falling demand in China, the world's largest car market.

Competitors Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen have both also issued profit warnings this year and, like BMW, plan job cuts to bring costs down.

In its latest warning, BMW said its redundancy program was moving faster than expected, resulting in bigger-than-anticipated severance payments for the final quarter of the year.

"The company intends to leverage the momentum generated by its workforce restructuring program to expand its organizational and process realignment more quickly," it said.

"The reduction in management functions will be implemented faster than announced," it added.

Strong demand for new models based on the firm's Neue Klasse platform meanwhile meant the company would incur charges to bring in extra shifts, it said.

Car and motorbike deliveries for the year are nevertheless expected to fall more steeply than expected, BMW said.

Across its brands -- which apart from the namesake include Mini and Rolls-Royce -- BMW last year delivered a total 2.46 million vehicles.

BMW reports its results for the third quarter on Wednesday.

articles.title: Reddit tests ads in search results as traffic declines and growth concerns mount
articles.summary: The new ad placements could help Reddit squeeze more revenue from existing users as Google's AI search changes how people discover its content.
articles.body:
Just days after warning investors about declining search traffic and a weaker-than-expected revenue forecast, Reddit is looking for more ways to make money from its existing users. On Tuesday, the company announced that it's beginning to test ad placements in its search results pages, allowing advertisers to reach users as they search for products, recommendations, and other information on its platform.

"Ads in search may appear based on a range of factors, including contextual relevance to a user's search query," Reddit shared in its announcement about the new ad placements. "This is an initial test with a select group of eligible advertisers. During this test, we will evaluate and understand how users respond to these ads so we can refine the experience for users and advertisers over time."

The company offered examples of what sort of ads might appear, suggesting that a search for "espresso station" might display ads for espresso machines, coffee, or mugs, while a search for "home office setup" could surface ads for things like monitors, desks, and office chairs.

The ad test comes at a time when Reddit is reckoning with how AI has been changing the web's landscape, and subsequently its reach.

Despite beating Wall Street's estimates for revenue and earnings per share, the company's stock dropped after it reported its third-quarter results last week , with fourth-quarter guidance that predicted sales of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, below expectations of $1.05 billion. This was tied to Reddit's declining search traffic referrals resulting from Google's move to an AI-powered search experience. AI search now sends less traffic to publishers' websites, as features like AI Mode provide answers directly on Google's Search Result pages, reducing clicks to other websites.

Reddit also said that its global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in the quarter, and were down 2% year-over-year. The company noted that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low double-digit percentage by the fourth quarter.

This leaves the company needing to earn more revenue from its existing users, which is where these new ads come in. The ads could prove to be more valuable to Reddit after it makes its planned shift to a logged-in experience, which was also announced during earnings. The company said it will make the transition gradually, initially in markets outside the U.S.

articles.title: Pre-Diwali fireworks: Sensex up over 2.4k points in two days
articles.summary: MUMBAI: For the second consecutive session on Tuesday, sensex notched up over a 1,000-point gain as relatively softer crude oil prices, strong foreign
articles.body: MUMBAI: For the second consecutive session on Tuesday, sensex notched up over a 1,000-point gain as relatively softer crude oil prices, strong foreign fund buying, softening yields in the US and a strengthening rupee helped investor sentiment on Dalal Street. After opening on a sound footing, sensex rallied through the session to close 1,225 points or 1.6% up at 76,918 points.Combined with a 1,233-point gain on Monday, the index is now up 2,458 points or 3.3%, the index's best two-day gaining streak since April 8 this year. The gains came on the back of nearly Rs 10,000-crore net buying by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) in the secondary market in two sessions.On Tuesday, sensex opened the session up about 600 points, touched an intraday high of 77,093 points (up 1,400 points) and closed just a tad off that level at 76,918 points. On NSE, Nifty too followed a similar trajectory and closed at 23,811 points, up 370 points or 1.6%. Ahead of Diwali this weekend, Tuesday was the fourth straight session of gains for the index.According to Ankur Punj, MD, Equirus Wealth, domestic markets rallied sharply as the easing West Asia conflict and falling crude oil prices coupled with encouraging Q2 earnings by corporates buoyed investor sentiment. "Despite weak global cues, domestic equities witnessed frenzied buying while fresh FII buying over the past two sessions and the rupee's recovery against the dollar provided impetus to the market."During the day, Brent crude prices fell to about the $103-per-barrel level, down 1.3%. Last week, Brent hit the $117 level, which in turn had weakened the rupee to near the 96-to-a-dollar mark. On Tuesday, the rupee strengthened 16 paise to close at 94.73 to the dollar.On Tuesday, net buying by foreign funds in the secondary market was at Rs 6,837 crore, exchange data showed. Domestic funds, on the other hand, were net sellers at Rs 3,679 crore. The day's strong foreign fund inflow came on the back of a Rs 3,115 crore net inflow in stocks on Monday. The day's strong gains in the market added about Rs 4.5 lakh crore to investors' wealth, with the aggregate market capitalisation of companies listed on BSE now at Rs 486.8 lakh crore, exchange data showed.HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Bharti Airtel contributed the most to the day's gain in the index.You use AI every day. articles.title: Won't open up dairy sector or let in genetically modified products: Piyush Goyal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With India, US close to finalising a trade, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal Tuesday said India has never opened up its dairy sector
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With India, US close to finalising a trade, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal Tuesday said India has never opened up its dairy sector in any free trade agreement and will not allow imports of genetically modified products, describing both as "very sensitive" issues for the country.Addressing students of Kirori Mal College, Goyal said India has "never ever" compromised on any sensitive item and has always protected its farmers, fishermen, and MSMEs in trade pacts."We are sensitive to opening up to certain agricultural produce, certain goods that we are very strong on like marine products. We are very sensitive to opening our dairy. In fact, till date, we have never opened up dairy for anybody. We are very sensitive not to allow any genetically modified products to come to India and we have never allowed it and we'll never allow it in the future," he said.He said, "We are sensitive to our religious sensitivities. So very often in foreign countries, they use calf meat or Rennet while producing their dairy products. We don't allow that in India. It is strictly got to be certified... so that religious sensitivities of the large parts of India are not hurt."Rennet is an enzyme used in cheese-making, traditionally obtained from the stomach lining of young calves. articles.title: SBI net rises 14% to 23k crore, shares slip 1.8%
articles.summary: MUMBAI: State Bank of India's Q2FY27 net profit rose 14.3% to Rs 23,038 crore, driven by a 14.7% increase in net interest income to Rs 49,143 crore and
articles.body: MUMBAI: State Bank of India's Q2FY27 net profit rose 14.3% to Rs 23,038 crore, driven by a 14.7% increase in net interest income to Rs 49,143 crore and lower loan loss provisions. Net interest margin improved to 3.1% from just over 3% a year ago, while loan loss provisions fell 33% to Rs 2,759 crore as asset quality improved.However, the bank's shares fell 1.8% to Rs 969 as investors were disappointed with the 7.3% growth in operating profit to Rs 34,226 crore. The increase was held back by a 24% decline in other income to Rs 11,777 crore.Addressing newspersons, SBI chairman CS Setty reiterated the bank's guidance of 10-11% deposit growth and 14-15% credit growth. The bank has a corporate loan pipeline of Rs 7.8 lakh crore, he said."If nominal GDP growth is around 12 to 12.5%, normally the SBI credit growth rate is 3 to 4% over that and that is where the guidance of 14 to 15% is coming from," explained Setty.The bank does not face any immediate compulsion to raise deposit rates, given its comfortable liquidity position. SBI had excess statutory liquidity ratio (SLR) holdings of more than Rs 4 lakh crore as of Sept 30, providing adequate headroom to fund credit growth, he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: LTCG tax abolition may cost Rs 40k-50k crore
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Government could abolish long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax across investor categories even keeping its fiscal consolidation road map largely
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Government could abolish long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax across investor categories even keeping its fiscal consolidation road map largely unaffected, as the resulting revenue loss is likely to be limited to Rs 40,000-50,000 crore in FY28, a report said on Tuesday.The report from SBI Research estimated that eliminating LTCG tax would reduce govt revenue by nearly 0.1-0.2% of GDP, a level it said could be absorbed while keeping fiscal deficit targets broadly on track. "We believe govt would be able to take this hit if hypothetically, the entire capital gains taxes were abolished," the report said. It estimated LTCG collections at around Rs 1 lakh crore in FY26 and projected them to decline to Rs 40,000-50,000 crore in FY27.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Noise and Gaana have announced the launch of the Noise Buds R1 (Gaana Edition), a co-branded product that brings together audio technology and music streaming in one offering.Priced at Rs 1,399, the earbuds come with a one-year Gaana Plus subscription. The launch brings together two homegrown brands seeking to make music streaming more accessible to consumers. "With music continuing to be a key part of everyday digital entertainment in India, the collaboration combines the convenience of wireless audio with the benefits of a premium music-streaming experience," said a statement.You use AI every day.
